impact: The cross-provider resume guard (session tracker preflight comparing the session's recorded provider to the active backend) lives only in the MCP tool layer (src/tools/* via createSessionTracker). The CLI (src/cli/commands.ts) calls the backend directly with no tracker, so `--session` with a session owned by the other provider is never rejected cleanly — it routes to the primary, which either hard-fails (dead binary: PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, observed live 2026-07-01) or would produce a confusing thread-not-found/new-thread behavior from the wrong provider's SDK. Cross-layer trust violation: the guard is assumed to exist below the surface layers, but only one of the two surface layers has it. Fix: move the guard into the backend/composite seam (or share the tracker preflight with CLI handlers) so both surfaces get the same clean rejection.
resolution: Fixed in T-027. Extracted a read-only checkSessionProvider guard shared by the MCP tracker and the CLI. The CLI now opens a read-only db (openReviewDb({readonly:true}), never creating/writing) and runs the guard before each review, so a foreign session_id gets the same PROVIDER_MISMATCH rejection (exit 1) as MCP. CLI records nothing (out of scope). Real-seeded-db CLI guard test in commands.test.ts. Note: the guard is cwd-dependent (fail-open otherwise) — tracked as ISS-018.
title: CLI resume path has no cross-provider session guard — foreign session_id surfaces as raw provider error
